title: Flat-term tensor and the strict open-kernel cochain diagram
statement:
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow P$ be an open immersion of schemes and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Work with integer cochain complexes of ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Apply the exact inverse-image adjunction $j^*\dashv j_*$ termwise [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact, lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy], writing $r_K=\eta_K:K\to j_*j^*K$, $S(K)=\ker r_K$ and $s_K:S(K)\to K$ for every complex $K$.

Let $Q,I,J$ be arbitrary, possibly unbounded cochain complexes on $P$, with every $Q^p$ flat, meaning that tensoring sheaves with $Q^p$ is exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Write $Q\otimes K=\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes_A K)$ for direct-sum total tensor, with differential $d_Q\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_K$ on bidegree $(p,q)$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Let $a:Q\otimes I\to J$ be any $A$-linear chain map. Put $C=j_*j^*I$, $C'=j_*j^*J$, and let $c_{Q,K}:j^*(Q\otimes K)\xrightarrow{\sim}j^*Q\otimes j^*K$ be the canonical cochain comparison [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]. Define
$$h=j^*a\,c_{Q,I}^{-1}(1\otimes\varepsilon^0_{j^*I})c_{Q,C},\qquad v=j_*h\,\eta_{Q\otimes C}:Q\otimes C\longrightarrow C',$$
where $\varepsilon^0:j^*j_*\to1$ is the ordinary counit and compositions are read right to left.

The map $v$ is a chain map, satisfies $v(1\otimes r_I)=r_Ja$, and on each total-degree summand is the ordinary adjunct of the displayed formula for $h$ on that summand. There is a unique chain map $u:Q\otimes S(I)\to S(J)$ satisfying $s_Ju=a(1\otimes s_I)$. Thus $(u,a,v)$ is a strict morphism of the two kernel rows. If $r_I$ and $r_J$ are degreewise epimorphisms, then
$$0\to Q\otimes S(I)\to Q\otimes I\to Q\otimes C\to0,\qquad 0\to S(J)\to J\to C'\to0$$
are degreewise short exact sequences. The construction is natural even without these epimorphism hypotheses: for complexes $I',J'$, a chain map $a':Q\otimes I'\to J'$, and maps $f:I\to I'$, $g:J\to J'$ with $ga=a'(1\otimes f)$, the induced maps between kernel rows commute with $(u,a,v)$ and $(u',a',v')$. This is a statement about actual $A$-linear cochain maps; neither K-flatness nor any second coefficient-ring action is assumed.

Apply the kernel universal property in the category of complexes to construct the unique u. Thus its chain equation is automatic; uniqueness follows by cancelling the kernel inclusion.

source.place: Tag 03DA, lemma-abelian, kernel universal property; functorial total tensor

proof.text: When restriction is degreewise epic, the kernel sequence is short exact and its evaluation in every degree is short exact. For the top total row in degree n, form the Discrete diagram indexed by pairs (p,q) with p+q=n, with row Q^p tensor row(I)^q. Flatness and the braiding make every component short exact. Evaluation detects exactness in the functor category, using mapHomologyIso. The coproduct functor preserves short exactness by the Grothendieck abelian AB4 instances and ShortExact.map_of_exact. The coproduct row is identified with the degree-n total tensor row by its coproduct injections.

For kernel maps, compose both proposed paths with the final kernel inclusion, use kernel.lift_ι, the defining equations for u,u', and the hypothesis a followed by g equals (1 tensor f) followed by a'; cancel the inclusion. Specialize the proved generic diagram to the ordinary etale upperStarLowerStarAdjunction.
